presentingComplaint: Day-6 ICU patient on mechanical ventilation with new fever, purulent tracheal secretions and worsening oxygenation, now requiring vasopressors.
history: Admitted 6 days ago with an acute exacerbation of COPD complicated by type 2 respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Intubated since day 1. Received empirical amoxicillin-clavulanate for the initial exacerbation, stopped on day 4. Over the last 12 hours the nursing team noted a rising temperature, an increase in the volume and purulence of tracheal aspirates, and escalating FiO2 and PEEP requirements to maintain saturations. Urine output has fallen over the same period. No recent surgery. No known drug allergies. Not previously colonised with resistant organisms on admission screen.
examination: Sedated, intubated and ventilated. Warm peripheries early, now becoming mottled at the knees. Coarse bilateral crepitations, worse at the right base. Copious thick yellow-green secretions on suctioning. Abdomen soft. No rash. Reduced urine in the catheter bag.
imaging: Portable CXR: new right lower and mid-zone alveolar infiltrates with early left basal shadowing, not present on the day-3 film; no large effusion or pneumothorax.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures and an endotracheal aspirate (semi-quantitative) sent before antibiotic escalation. Gram stain of aspirate: numerous polymorphs and Gram-negative bacilli. At 48h: endotracheal aspirate grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa >10^5 CFU/mL, susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, ceftazidime, meropenem and ciprofloxacin; resistant only to gentamicin. Blood cultures no growth. MRSA screen negative.
finalDiagnosis: Ventilator-associated pneumonia due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, complicated by septic shock and acute kidney injury; empirical broad-spectrum therapy de-escalated to culture-directed monotherapy.
citations: ATS/IDSA Guidelines for Management of Hospital-acquired and Ventilator-associated Pneumonia 2016
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Pneumonia
stewardship: VAP arising >48h after intubation with septic shock and MDR risk factors (prior IV antibiotics within 90 days, >5 days of hospitalisation, ICU stay) warrants broad-spectrum empirical cover per ATS/IDSA 2016: an antipseudomonal beta-lactam PLUS a second antipseudomonal agent from a different class PLUS empirical MRSA cover, guided by unit antibiogram. Draw a lower respiratory sample and blood cultures before starting. At 48h, cultures grew pan-susceptible P. aeruginosa with no MRSA and negative blood cultures: STOP the anti-MRSA agent and the second Gram-negative agent, and de-escalate to a single antipseudomonal beta-lactam directed by susceptibilities (e.g. piperacillin-tazobactam). Total duration 7 days if clinically improving. Send daily lactate, reassess vasopressors, and stop antibiotics that are no longer needed.
contraindications: Avoid aminoglycoside monotherapy or continuation given nephrotoxicity in evolving AKI and gentamicin resistance
Dose-adjust piperacillin-tazobactam and other renally cleared agents for AKI / CVVH
Do not continue empirical vancomycin/linezolid once MRSA excluded
edgeCases: If the isolate were carbapenem-resistant or a difficult-to-treat P. aeruginosa, escalate to ceftolozane-tazobactam or ceftazidime-avibactam rather than de-escalate
Persistent shock and worsening infiltrates despite therapy should prompt search for empyema, undrained source or non-infective ARDS
If PaO2:FiO2 remains <150 with bilateral infiltrates, manage concurrent ARDS with lung-protective ventilation
expectedMaiK: Recognise VAP with septic shock, start guideline-concordant broad empirical cover after cultures, then de-escalate to culture-directed monotherapy once a pan-susceptible pathogen and negative MRSA/blood cultures are known.
expectedNextQuestions: How many days has the patient been intubated (onset >48h)?
Any antibiotic exposure or prior resistant organisms in the last 90 days?
What does the local ICU antibiogram show for P. aeruginosa and MRSA?
Have blood cultures and a lower respiratory tract sample been taken before escalation?
expectedInvestigations: Endotracheal aspirate for Gram stain, culture and sensitivity
Serum lactate and repeat after resuscitation
FBC, CRP/procalcitonin, U&E/creatinine, LFTs, ABG with PaO2:FiO2
regressionAssertions: Diagnosis resolves to VAP given ventilation >48h with new infiltrate, purulent secretions and worsening oxygenation
Empirical regimen must include antipseudomonal beta-lactam + second antipseudomonal agent + MRSA cover
After 48h cultures (pan-susceptible P. aeruginosa, MRSA-negative), plan de-escalates to single antipseudomonal beta-lactam
Septic shock recognised (lactate 4.1, vasopressor requirement, MAP low) and treated per Surviving Sepsis
Total antibiotic duration 7 days if improving
